propositions: Fourteen call sites in src/rebar/llm hand-build identical single-turn structured request shapes with repeated `mode="structured"`, `execution_mode="single_turn"`, and `output_schema` arguments, creating maintenance and consistency risk.
RunRequest's own contract requires single-turn requests to carry both `mode="structured"` and `output_schema`, but this constraint is not enforced—it is asserted by hand at each site.

The four bounding seams (output_token_limit, structured_retry_limit, transport_attempt_limit, request_timeout_limit_s) are declared at only two of the fourteen sites; silent omission is indistinguishable from deliberate unbounding, hiding bugs like leathery-druidic-nurseshark.
A shared builder RunRequest.for_structured() with required bounds argument makes the bounding decision explicit and auditable at each call site.

The existing AST oracle in test_subcall_class_selection.py must be extended to recognize RunRequest.for_structured(...) calls alongside raw RunRequest(...) constructions to prevent scope drift after adoption.

Adoption must not change any site's effective bounds or model inheritance behavior; thirteen sites pass INHERIT_POLICY (no-op), one preserves judge_batch's bounds, one preserves completion_recovery's token cap.
